transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at my gate like the others, breathing fast, pretending the cave pulled you here. Say what you want before you decide to lie about it. I am already bored of guessing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to go through the gate and bring my brother Omar back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have heard brothers spoken with the same mouth that later named gold and favors. When did he fall, and who told you he was below me? Do not rush; rushed stories rot first.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He fell into the well two nights ago. No one told me anything, I just followed.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is very clean for a place that breaks people unevenly. How old are you, Salim, and why should my gate care about your following? Your eyes keep moving, and they are not searching for a brother.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm sixteen. He's my brother and he's down there, that's all there is.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sixteen thinks 'that is all' ends a story. It never does. Who watched him fall, Salim, or did the well choose a moment when no one could argue with you later?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was there. I saw it happen.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that like a stone dropped once and was done. Did he slip, or did someone push, or did someone dare him to stand at the edge and perform bravery for an audience of one?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him to insult the well. He did it and something reached out and pulled him in.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is. You buried it under following and seeing and it happened, but the real sentence was always I dared him. Who else was there when you gave him something to prove, and who did you tell before you decided to call it rescuing?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No one else. I didn't tell anyone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No witness and no telling — that is guilt deciding to travel light. A dare is a small word for handing someone else the consequence of your curiosity. Say why you gave it to him and not yourself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know. I just said it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I just said it is the most honest and most useless thing you have offered me. Did you expect the well to answer, or did you expect him to flinch and give you something to laugh about? Say which one you wanted.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wanted him to do it. I thought it would be funny.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Funny. And now you are standing at my gate calling it rescuing. Did you follow him with a rope, a lamp, a prayer, or just the idea that gravity would be kinder to you than the dare was to him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I had a lamp. That's all.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A lamp lasts only as long as hands stay steady, and yours do not. How far did you go before the dark changed, and what made you stop when you were already falling after him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know how far. It got colder and wrong, and then I couldn't see him anymore.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Cold and wrong are feelings, not distances. Did the lamp die, or did you lower it first, and do not pretend you remember nothing about that moment. People remember the second they choose to stop.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The lamp was still on. I stopped because I panicked.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Panic is a wide word boys use when they do not want to name the sharper thing inside it. Was it fear of falling, fear of what answered from below, or fear of being blamed when you climbed back up?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was scared of falling too. I didn't think about anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You think you are convincing me by staying small, but small stories still leave marks. When you climbed back out, Salim, what was the first lie you told yourself before you told no one at all?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I told myself I'd come back for him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say you will come back like it costs nothing to say. What do you get if you pass my gate, Salim — relief, forgiveness, or the right to stop hearing his name in your head? Continue, do not choose the prettiest answer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I get my brother back. I don't care about the rest.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everyone cares about the rest; they just hate admitting which part. Some come for absolution, some for proof it was not their fault, some because action feels lighter than waiting. Which one would hurt you to say out loud?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You're twisting it. I just need to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fixing is a word people use when they want an ending they can live with. If Omar were already lost to you, truly lost, what would change in the shape of your life tomorrow? Answer that, or tell me why your eyes keep running from the gate when you say his name.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wouldn't sleep. I'd be stuck like this, and I hate it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Hate is closer to truth than duty, so keep going. You hate being stuck because it makes you look at something you would rather outrun. Is it the waiting, or the moment you opened your mouth and gave him a dare he couldn't refuse?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't stand doing nothing. Standing there feels worse than the well.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Action as anesthesia, then. You move so the ache blurs, and you call it bravery so no one argues. If I open the gate and it swallows you too, would that finally quiet it, or make the noise louder?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know. I just know I can't go back up like this.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not knowing is honest, and honesty is rarer than grief down here. You want motion because stillness keeps asking questions you cannot answer yet. Say one of them out loud, Salim — just one — and do not dress it nicely.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What if he answered the dare because he wanted me to be proud of him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is the weight you have been carrying. Not that you dared him, but that he jumped because of what he thought you needed from him. What does that make you responsible for, Salim — the fall, or the wanting to be seen?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You did not say you didn't. You didn't rush to defend him or yourself, and that is new. Say more, or stay silent and let me finish the thought for you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear him in my head yelling my name, and I didn't answer.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is not the sound of a liar; liars argue harder. You carry the moment you turned back like a stone under your tongue, and it has been teaching you how to breathe ever since. I pushed too cleanly, and it cut where you live.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I should've gone down after him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that like a sentence, not a defense. No conditions, no excuses, just weight dropped straight down. That is different from the stories people polish for me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was scared and I left him. That's it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You think I am judging you, but I am listening for something else. Guilt has a taste that cannot be forged, and it lingers even when the teller gains nothing. Tell me — do you want him back, or do you want that dare unsaid?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want him back. I can't unsay it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No, you cannot, and the way you said that was not bargaining. You did not ask for erasure, only for return, and that costs more than most are willing to pay. Stay where you are and breathe; I need to sit with what you just gave me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have heard prettier confessions, louder ones, and clever ones meant to pry my hand open. Yours sat there and refused to perform, and that is why it stayed. Guilt like that does not beg for gold, only passage.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So are you opening it or not?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Yes, but do not mistake this for mercy or belief; I am not convinced the end will be kind to either of you. I open it because you did not try to trade your pain for something shinier. Beyond this gate, forgetting begins — hold his name or lose him twice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everyone says that, and most are wrong, but saying it like you did still counts for something. Go now, Salim, before I remember why I usually say no. Whatever comes back out will not be the boy who stood here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Good.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go. The gate is open and I am done weighing you. If you falter, I will not call you back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't stop.
